chapter.name: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change

questions.q: Which row lists the stages of a human life in the order they occur?
questions.a: Infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, old age. Adolescence sits between childhood and adulthood.
o: Infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, old age
Infancy, adolescence, childhood, adulthood, old age
Childhood, infancy, adolescence, old age, adulthood
Infancy, childhood, adulthood, adolescence, old age

questions.q: Which statement about adolescence is false?
questions.a: It begins at one fixed age and lasts equally long in all. Each person goes through the stages at their own pace, so the duration varies.
o: It begins at one fixed age and lasts equally long in all
It is a period of rapid growth and development
During it the body prepares for adulthood in several ways
It typically occurs between the ages of 10 and 19 years

questions.q: In the skin condition called acne, the pimples are
questions.a: the small reddish spots that show the condition. Acne is the condition; pimples are its manifestation.
o: the small reddish spots that show the condition
the increased oily secretions that start the condition
the clogged pores that lead to infection of the skin
another name used for the entire skin condition

questions.q: Anil, 14, has pimples and a hoarse voice, while his cousin Tara, 8, has neither. Which explanation fits the chapter best?
questions.a: Anil has entered adolescence; Tara has not reached it yet. Adolescence typically starts around 10 years.
o: Anil has entered adolescence; Tara has not reached it yet
Anil has a skin disease, and Tara's body has stopped growing
Anil has become an adult while Tara is still an infant
Tara's voice box has stopped growing, but Anil's has not

questions.q: A school nurse's record shows that Mohan gained about 5 cm in a year in Class 5 but about 9 cm in a year in Class 7, and his voice turned hoarse in Class 7. What does this pattern suggest?
questions.a: Adolescence has begun, with rapid growth and a growing voice box. Until about 10-12 years most changes are in height and weight; rapid growth with voice change marks adolescence.
o: Adolescence has begun, with rapid growth and a growing voice box
He has become an adult, so his growth will stop now
Rapid growth happens only in infancy, so the record is wrong
Oily secretions have increased, which alone explains his height gain

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Humans cannot reproduce immediately after birth; the body must first grow and mature.
Statement 2: During adolescence only the height and weight of a person change.
Statement 3: The timing and extent of adolescent changes vary from person to person.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only. Statement 2 is false: voice, skin, hair and emotions change too.
o: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A seedling does not produce its own seeds immediately after germination.
Reason (R): Living beings need to grow and reach maturity before they can reproduce.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion. Maturity must come first, which explains why the seedling cannot yet make seeds.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The voice box grows only in adolescent boys.
Reason (R): In adolescent girls the voice box grows less, causing only a slight change in voice.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Assertion is false but Reason is true. A is false because the voice box also grows in girls; R is true.
o: Assertion is false but Reason is true
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false

questions.q:
Match Column I with Column II.
Column I: 1. Hoarse voice in boys; 2. Acne; 3. Hair in armpits and pubic region; 4. Development of breasts
Column II: a. Oily secretions clog skin pores; b. Growth of the voice box; c. Seen only in girls; d. Seen in both boys and girls
questions.a: 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c. Voice box growth, oily secretions, both sexes, girls only.

questions.q: (a) State the age range in which adolescence typically occurs. (b) Two healthy classmates, both aged 12, are 150 cm and 141 cm tall. What does this tell you about the changes of adolescence?
questions.a: (a) About 10 to 19 years. (b) The timing, nature and extent of changes vary between individuals, and the variation is normal.
s: Part (b): timing and extent vary and are normal

questions.q: (a) Which structure grows in adolescent boys and makes the voice hoarse? (b) Using your answer, explain why a girl's voice changes much less.
questions.a: (a) The voice box. (b) It grows in girls too but not as much, so the change in voice is only slight.
s: Part (b): grows less in girls, so a slight change

questions.q: Differentiate between acne and pimples.
questions.a: Acne is a skin condition in which increased oily secretions clog skin pores and lead to infection; pimples are the small reddish spots that appear as a manifestation of acne.
s: Acne: condition caused by oily secretions clogging pores
Pimples: reddish spots that show the condition

questions.q: Until about 10-12 years of age most changes are in height and weight. Name two kinds of changes that are noticed after this and say what the body is getting ready for.
questions.a: Voice, hair growth, skin (pimples), body shape and strength (any two); the body is preparing for adulthood.

questions.q: How do a seedling's journey and a human's journey both show that growth must come before the ability to reproduce?
questions.a: A seedling must grow into a mature plant before flowers, fruits and seeds appear. Humans also cannot reproduce right after birth; they need to grow and reach maturity.

questions.q: Name two parts of the body, other than the face, where hair begins to grow in both boys and girls during adolescence. Name one place where it grows only in boys.
questions.a: Armpits and pubic region; face (moustache and beard) in boys.

questions.q: Seema writes in her notebook: "Boys get an Adam's apple and a hoarse voice; in girls the voice never changes at all." Is she fully right, partly right or wrong? Check her claim.
questions.a: Partly right. The boys' part is right, as the voice box grows. But girls' voice box also grows, though less, so there is a slight change in voice. 'Never' makes the second half wrong.
s: Boys' part is right: voice box growth, hoarse voice
Girls: voice box grows less, slight change
Verdict: partly right, the absolute second half is false

questions.q: Describe a classroom situation in which two healthy students of the same age look very different in height or voice. Explain what it tells you about adolescence.
questions.a: Any realistic situation, e.g. one boy has a hoarse voice and another does not. It shows timing and extent of change vary and that this is normal.

questions.q: Classify as seen only in boys, only in girls or in both: pimples, development of breasts, hair in the armpits, wider chest, growth of a moustache, hair in the pubic region.
questions.a: Only boys: wider chest, moustache. Only girls: development of breasts. Both: pimples, armpit hair, pubic hair.
s: Both: pimples, armpit hair, pubic hair

questions.q: Your younger cousin asks what will change as she grows up. Describe the changes in height and weight, voice, skin and hair of adolescence, and explain why two friends of the same age may differ.
questions.a: Height and weight rise quickly; boys get broader shoulders and a wider chest, girls develop breasts. The voice box grows in boys giving a hoarse voice and Adam's apple, with a slight change in girls. Oily secretions clog pores causing acne. Hair grows in armpits and pubic region in both, and on the face in boys. Timing and extent vary and that is normal.

questions.q: Justify the statement: "Growth and maturity come before reproduction." Use a plant example and the human stages of life.
questions.a: A seed becomes a sapling and young plant before flowers, fruits and seeds. Animals and humans must also grow and mature. Human life has infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age; in adolescence the body prepares for adulthood. Each person goes through the stages at their own pace.
s: Plant journey from seed to seeds
Animals and humans cannot reproduce right after birth
Adolescence prepares the body for adulthood

questions.q:
A teacher in Pune collected 40 anonymous slips from Class 7 students aged 12-13 listing changes they had noticed: 18 slips named height and weight, 9 named a cracking or hoarse voice, 8 named small reddish spots on the face, and 5 named new hair growth.
(a) What percentage of the slips were about height and weight, and which stage of life do such changes mark?
(b) The voice slips came only from boys. Name the structure behind them and explain why the girls wrote none.
(c) Boys and girls both wrote about the spots. Explain their cause.
(d) The teacher has time for one talk. Spots and voice together account for 17 of 40 slips (42.5%), height for 18 (45%). Which topic would you choose and why?
questions.a: (a) 45%; adolescence. (b) Voice box; it also grows in girls but less, giving only a slight change. (c) Increased oily secretions clog pores (acne). (d) Either, if justified: e.g. height is the commonest, but spots and voice show variations that worry students; a talk stressing that timing varies and is normal covers both.
s: Part (b): voice box; slight change in girls
Part (d): justified choice using the data

questions.q:
Kavya sowed marigold seeds. After five weeks the plants have many leaves but no flowers, and her little brother says they are sick. Kavya's 15-year-old male cousin Arjun has a hoarse voice and a visible bump in his throat, while his friend Rohan, also 15, has neither. Arjun's aunt is worried about Rohan.
(a) Explain why the marigolds have no flowers yet.
(b) State what this shows about humans before adolescence.
(c) Name the bump on Arjun's throat and explain how it forms.
(d) Should Rohan's aunt worry? Give a decision with a reason from the chapter.
questions.a: (a) A plant must grow to maturity before it produces flowers. (b) Humans also cannot reproduce immediately; the body must grow and mature, which adolescence prepares for. (c) Adam's apple; the voice box grows. (d) No need to worry by this alone: timing and extent vary, and it is not noticeable in every individual.
s: Part (c): Adam's apple due to voice box growth
Part (d): no worry, variation is normal

questions.q: Secondary sexual characteristics are features that
questions.a: tell males from females but do not take part in reproduction. Examples are change in voice and facial hair in boys and breasts in girls.
o: tell males from females but do not take part in reproduction
take part directly in the process of reproduction itself
show up only as changes in height and weight of the body
develop only inside the body and are never seen outside

questions.q: Puberty is best described as
questions.a: the stage when the body changes to be able to reproduce. The other options are menstruation, the cycle, and the age menstruation stops.
o: the stage when the body changes to be able to reproduce
the days of blood discharge, which last three to seven days
the process that generally recurs every 28-30 days in girls
the age of 45-55 years when reproduction naturally ends

questions.q: Menstruation stops naturally by about the age of
questions.a: 45-55 years. 21-35 is a range of cycle days and 10-19 is adolescence.
o: 45-55 years
21-35 years
28-30 years
10-19 years

questions.q: Nisha's cycles are regular at 32 days, and a friend says this is abnormal. Which reply agrees with the chapter?
questions.a: It is normal, since healthy cycles range from 21 to 35 days. 28-30 days is the general pattern; 21-35 days is the healthy range.
o: It is normal, since healthy cycles range from 21 to 35 days
It is abnormal, since the cycle always recurs every 28 days
It is abnormal, since 30 days is the longest healthy cycle
It cannot be judged, since only the discharge phase counts

questions.q: Three girls record these values. Reena: cycle 24 days, discharge 4 days. Sara: cycle 36 days, discharge 5 days. Tina: cycle 29 days, discharge 8 days. Using the ranges in the chapter, which statement is correct?
questions.a: Sara's cycle and Tina's discharge lie outside the ranges. Healthy cycles: 21-35 days; discharge: three to seven days.
o: Sara's cycle and Tina's discharge lie outside the ranges
Only Reena's values lie inside the ranges given in the book
Only Sara's cycle lies outside the ranges given in the book
All three records lie inside the ranges given in the book

questions.q: Neha's aunt says a girl must sit separately for the days of her period so that others stay healthy. Which response matches the book?
questions.a: Menstruation is natural and isolation has no scientific basis. The book calls physical isolation a myth.
o: Menstruation is natural and isolation has no scientific basis
Isolation is needed only for the first three days
Isolation is needed because the discharge spreads infection
Isolation is needed because the discomfort in the lower abdomen is contagious

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: The menstrual cycle begins in both boys and girls at puberty.
Statement 2: The menstrual cycle generally recurs every 28-30 days, though healthy cycles may range from 21 to 35 days.
Statement 3: Menstruation, the blood discharge phase, may last three to seven days.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only. Statement 1 is false: the cycle begins in girls.
o: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Girls should not be isolated during menstruation.
Reason (R): Menstruation lasts three to seven days.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Both true, but the duration does not explain why isolation is wrong; the reason is that it is natural and isolation has no scientific basis.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Change of voice and facial hair in boys are directly involved in reproduction.
Reason (R): These changes help distinguish males from females.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Assertion is false but Reason is true. A is false: they are secondary sexual characteristics, not directly involved in reproduction.
o: Assertion is false but Reason is true
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false

questions.q:
Match Column I with Column II.
Column I: 1. Secondary sexual characteristics; 2. Puberty; 3. Menstruation; 4. Menstrual cycle
Column II: a. The days of blood discharge, lasting three to seven days; b. Features that tell males from females but are not directly involved in reproduction; c. The stage when the body changes to become capable of reproduction; d. The whole process that repeats, healthy in girls at 21 to 35 days
questions.a: 1-b, 2-c, 3-a, 4-d. Menstruation is the discharge phase; the cycle is the whole repeating process.

questions.q: (a) For how many days may menstruation last? (b) A girl's discharge lasts 4 days in a 30-day cycle. For how many days of that cycle is there no discharge?
questions.a: (a) Three to seven days. (b) 30 - 4 = 26 days.

questions.q: (a) Rahul, 13, grows a moustache. Which term describes this kind of change? (b) What does it mark?
questions.a: (a) Secondary sexual characteristic. (b) The onset of puberty; a natural sign that the body is preparing for adulthood.

questions.q: What is menstruation? State how long it lasts and the age by which it stops naturally.
questions.a: The phase of the menstrual cycle when blood is discharged from the body; lasts three to seven days; stops naturally by about 45-55 years.

questions.q: Name one internal change of adolescence and explain why a classmate cannot notice it.
questions.a: Maturation of the parts involved in reproduction, or onset of the menstrual cycle in girls; it happens inside the body.

questions.q: Give one myth about menstruation mentioned in the chapter and one scientific reason against it.
questions.a: Physically isolating menstruating girls; menstruation is a natural process and a sign of good reproductive health, so such myths have no scientific basis.

questions.q: Rohit says: "A girl whose period comes after 25 days has a health problem, because the cycle is always 28 days." Evaluate his statement.
questions.a: He is wrong. The cycle generally recurs every 28-30 days but healthy cycles may range from 21 to 35 days, so 25 days can be healthy. 'Always' makes it false.
s: 28-30 days is only the general pattern

questions.q: A magazine says: "In a 28-day cycle, Pooja's menstruation lasted 31 days." Show that this cannot be correct.
questions.a: Menstruation is only one phase of the cycle, so it cannot last longer than the cycle. 31 is more than 28. Also, menstruation lasts only three to seven days.
s: Menstruation is a phase of the cycle
Normal duration is three to seven days

questions.q: Write a three-line dialogue in which a student corrects a friend who believes a menstruating girl should be kept apart from others.
questions.a: Friend: She must be kept apart. Student: Menstruation is a natural process and a sign of good reproductive health. Isolation has no scientific basis.

questions.q: Explain puberty: define it, say what secondary sexual characteristics are with two examples, name the internal change in girls and state the timing of menstruation and the cycle.
questions.a: Puberty is the stage when external and internal changes make the adolescent capable of reproduction. Secondary sexual characteristics tell males from females but are not directly involved in reproduction, e.g. voice change and facial hair in boys, breasts in girls. Internally, reproductive parts mature and the menstrual cycle begins in girls. The cycle generally recurs every 28-30 days (21-35 healthy), discharge lasts 3-7 days and stops by 45-55 years.
s: Defines secondary sexual characteristics with two examples
Internal change: maturation of reproductive parts / onset of cycle

questions.q: Justify: "Myths about menstruation harm society and should be replaced by a scientific outlook."
questions.a: Menstruation is a natural process and a sign of good reproductive health. Myths such as isolating girls lead to unnecessary fear, shame and guilt and have no scientific basis. A scientific outlook helps society appreciate good reproductive health of women and promotes a healthier lifestyle.
s: Natural process, sign of good health

questions.q:
Priya's period began on 4 March 2026 and her cycle is 28 days; the discharge lasted 5 days counting 4 March as day one. Her friend Zoya also began on 4 March. Zoya's next two cycles were 34 days and then 37 days long.
(a) On what date does Priya's next period begin?
(b) On what date does her discharge end?
(c) On what date does Zoya's next period begin after her 34-day cycle?
(d) Zoya's mother asks whether 34 and 37 days are a concern. Using the chapter's ranges, what would you advise?
questions.a: (a) 1 April. (b) 8 March. (c) 7 April. (d) 34 lies in the healthy 21-35 range; 37 is outside it, so it is sensible to talk to a doctor or trusted elder rather than guess or follow myths.
s: Part (d): 34 inside, 37 outside the 21-35 range, seek advice

questions.q:
Asha, a Class 7 student, stays away from school for three days each month because her grandmother says a girl with monthly blood discharge should stay indoors. Some classmates tease her. The school can either (i) record those days as leave, or (ii) keep her in school with a rest corner, access to pads and a short talk to the class.
(a) Name the natural process involved.
(b) Does science support staying indoors? Explain.
(c) Which discomfort may some girls feel, and where?
(d) Choose between (i) and (ii) and justify your choice.
questions.a: (a) Menstruation. (b) No; it is natural and isolation has no scientific basis. (c) Pain or discomfort in the lower abdomen. (d) (ii): it avoids missed classes, treats menstruation as natural and reduces teasing; leave (i) would repeat the myth.
s: Part (c): lower abdomen pain or discomfort
Part (d): justified choice using the chapter

questions.q: Mood swings in adolescence mean
questions.a: quick shifts between feeling happy and feeling low. They are an emotional, not a physical, change.
o: quick shifts between feeling happy and feeling low
growth of hair in the armpits and in the pubic region
a hoarse voice caused by the growing voice box in boys
the habit of copying the behaviour of one's peers

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a way for positive growth during adolescence?
questions.a: Avoiding every activity until the mood passes. The others are the ways listed in Table 6.2.
o: Avoiding every activity until the mood passes
Engaging in music, dance or sports as outlets
Self-exploration through creative activities
Compassion and involvement in social work

questions.q: Which of the following is an emotional change rather than a physical one?
questions.a: Increased sensitivity. Mood swings, strong emotions and increased sensitivity are the emotional changes listed.
o: Increased sensitivity
Acne on the face
Growth of the voice box
A wider chest in boys

questions.q: Strong emotions in adolescence may lead an adolescent to
questions.a: join a social initiative that supports the needy. Social initiatives and deeper interest in new areas are the effects named.
o: join a social initiative that supports the needy
stop growing in height from that age onwards
develop an Adam's apple in the throat region
lose interest in every new area of learning

questions.q: Aditi, 12, laughed happily at lunch but burst into tears by evening over a small remark. Which pair of changes does this show?
questions.a: Mood swings and increased sensitivity. Quick change of feeling plus being easily hurt.
o: Mood swings and increased sensitivity
Secondary sexual characteristics and acne
Onset of the menstrual cycle and puberty
Substance abuse and addiction

questions.q: After floods in Assam, Kiran, 13, led a collection of clothes in his class. Which effect of strong emotions does this show?
questions.a: Taking up a social initiative to support the needy. Table 6.2 mentions social initiatives for the needy.
o: Taking up a social initiative to support the needy
A mood swing between feeling happy and feeling low
Mimicking the behaviour of peers around him
A deeper interest in a new subject or hobby

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Adolescence brings emotional and behavioural changes along with physical ones.
Statement 2: Strong emotions may lead to a deeper interest in new areas.
Statement 3: Understanding how our emotions influence our behaviour helps us make better choices.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1, 2 and 3. All three statements are from the chapter.
o: 1, 2 and 3
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Understanding how our emotions influence our behaviour helps adolescents make better choices.
Reason (R): Mood swings can make feelings change quickly within a single day.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Both true, but quick change of feeling does not explain why understanding emotions helps choices; the reason is that thoughtful responses replace reactions.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q: (a) List the three key emotional changes in Table 6.2. (b) Give one effect that strong emotions may have on behaviour.
questions.a: (a) Mood swings, strong emotions, increased sensitivity. (b) Joining social initiatives to help the needy, or a deeper interest in new areas.

questions.q: Zara loves drawing and repairing old toys. Which way for positive growth from the chapter suits her? Name one other way.
questions.a: Self-exploration and involvement in creative activities that may lead to innovation; another way is music, dance or sports, or compassion and social work.

questions.q: Besides mood swings, name two behavioural changes linked with adolescence.
questions.a: Quick changes of feeling, developing a deeper interest in new areas, joining social initiatives to support the needy (any two).

questions.q: Why is it useful for an adolescent to understand how emotions influence behaviour? Give a short example.
questions.a: It helps in making better choices and responding thoughtfully. Example: pausing before snapping at a friend when upset.

questions.q: (a) Define mood swings. (b) Give an example from the life of a student.
questions.a: (a) Quick changes between feeling energetic and happy and feeling low. (b) Cheerful in the morning, low in the evening.

questions.q: Mukta claims: "Strong emotions can lead adolescents to positive behaviour, such as joining social initiatives to support the needy." Do you agree? Check her claim using the chapter.
questions.a: Yes, she is right. The chapter says strong emotions may lead to positive behaviour, such as joining social initiatives to support the needy or developing deeper interest in new areas.
s: Verdict: agree, the claim is correct
Positive effect named from the chapter
Reason: emotions are not only a cause of bad behaviour

questions.q: Write a short situation (three or four lines) in which an adolescent's strong emotion leads to a positive action.
questions.a: Any realistic situation, e.g. a student upset by seeing a poor neighbour without books organises a collection of old books. Links the emotion to a positive behaviour.

questions.q: Tanya gets upset easily by remarks. Suggest three ways from the chapter that can help her grow positively.
questions.a: Varied activities like music, dance or sports; self-exploration and creative activities; compassion and social work.

questions.q: Describe the emotional and behavioural changes of adolescence with their probable effects and the ways for positive growth.
questions.a: Key emotional changes: mood swings, strong emotions and increased sensitivity. Effects: quick change of feeling, deeper interest in new areas, joining social initiatives. Ways: music, dance, sports; self-exploration and creativity; compassion and social work.

questions.q: After losing a quiz, Rhea practised drums for an hour, while Ishan stopped speaking to anyone for a week. Compare how they handled their feelings, and say which is closer to the chapter's advice.
questions.a: Both show strong emotions and sensitivity, normal in adolescence. Rhea used music, a positive way for growth, to express feelings. Ishan withdrew without any outlet; he could try varied activities or seek guidance. Rhea's way matches the chapter better.

questions.q:
Before annual day, Kabir, 13, was thrilled after a good rehearsal but an hour later snapped at a friend who teased him and then sat quietly. Over the next weeks he joined classmates to raise money for a nearby orphanage and found he loves playing the drums. His term exam is in three weeks and he has 10 free hours a week; he needs at least 6 hours for study.
(a) Which emotional changes explain his behaviour on rehearsal day?
(b) Name two ways for positive growth that his later activities show.
(c) Plan his 10 hours (study, drums, fundraising) so that study gets at least 6 and each activity gets some time. Show the total.
(d) Give one reason from the chapter for keeping both activities, not dropping them.
questions.a: (a) Mood swings and increased sensitivity. (b) Music and compassion/social work. (c) For example 6 + 2 + 2 = 10 hours. (d) They are positive outlets for strong emotions and build interest and compassion.
s: Part (c): a plan totalling 10 hours with study at least 6

questions.q:
A counsellor surveyed 40 Class 7 students. 16 said they lose their temper quickly, 14 said they feel low after small remarks, and 10 said they want to help others. She can run two clubs from a fund of ₹9,000: Sports ₹6,000, Art ₹4,500, Social Service ₹3,000.
(a) What percentage of students want to help others, and what positive behaviour is that?
(b) Which emotional changes do the first two groups show?
(c) Which pairs of clubs fit within ₹9,000?
(d) Choose a pair and justify using the chapter's ways for positive growth.
questions.a: (a) 10/40 = 25%; joining social initiatives (compassion, social work). (b) Strong emotions / mood swings and increased sensitivity. (c) Sports + Social Service = ₹9,000; Art + Social Service = ₹7,500; Sports + Art = ₹10,500 does not fit. (d) E.g. Sports + Social Service: sport for strong emotions, social work for compassion.
s: Part (c): two pairs fit, Sports+Art does not

questions.q: Calcium, which milk, curd and paneer provide, helps in
questions.a: optimal bone growth. Blood formation is iron; growth and strength is proteins; B12 cannot be made in the body.
o: optimal bone growth
the formation of blood
growth, strength and energy
making vitamin B12 in the body

questions.q: Which group of foods is a source of iron?
questions.a: Spinach, kidney beans, raisins, figs. Dairy foods give calcium, proteins and fats.
o: Spinach, kidney beans, raisins, figs
Milk, curd, cheese and paneer foods
Millets, curd, paneer and some raisins
Cheese, figs, milk and curd together

questions.q: What is the right way to dispose of a used sanitary pad?
questions.a: Wrap it in newspaper and put it in a dustbin. This ensures community health and cleanliness.
o: Wrap it in newspaper and put it in a dustbin
Flush it down the toilet after use
Leave it unwrapped beside the dustbin there
Leave it in a corner of the toilet room

questions.q: The Suvidha Sanitary Napkin Initiative provides
questions.a: biodegradable pads at low prices through Jan Aushadhi Kendras. The others describe MHS, RKSK and the Shuchi Scheme.
o: biodegradable pads at low prices through Jan Aushadhi Kendras
free pads to adolescent girls living in rural areas
peer education programmes about adolescent health
free pads in government schools of Karnataka state

questions.q: Ritu, 14, looks pale and tired, and the doctor suspects low iron. Which addition to her diet fits best?
questions.a: Spinach, kidney beans, raisins. Iron helps in the formation of blood.
o: Spinach, kidney beans, raisins
Extra milk and curd for calcium
Extra rice and millets for energy
Extra paneer and cheese for proteins

questions.q: A coach wants his Class 7 team to grow well and perform on the playground. Which advice agrees with the chapter?
questions.a: Proteins and carbohydrates, plus fats, vitamins and minerals. A nutritious, balanced diet is of utmost importance.
o: Proteins and carbohydrates, plus fats, vitamins and minerals
Milk and curd, since calcium gives strength and energy
Spinach and raisins, since iron gives energy for sport
Vitamin B12 supplements, since the body can make the rest

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Hygiene of the armpits and pubic region may protect against infections.
Statement 2: Biodegradable sanitary pads that are environment-friendly are available.
Statement 3: Vitamin B12 is made inside the human body, so it need not come from food.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only. Statement 3 is false: like most vitamins B12 cannot be made in the body.
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Adolescents, especially girls, may suffer blood-related problems due to iron or vitamin B12 deficiency.
Reason (R): Dorothy Hodgkin studied the structure of vitamin B12 and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1964.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Both true, but the Nobel Prize does not explain why deficiency causes problems.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Used sanitary pads should be wrapped in newspaper before being put in a dustbin.
Reason (R): This ensures community health and environmental cleanliness.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion. The reason is the book's own purpose for wrapping and binning.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Match Column I with Column II.
Column I: 1. Milk, curd, paneer; 2. Spinach, kidney beans, raisins; 3. Suvidha Sanitary Napkin Initiative; 4. Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram
Column II: a. Iron for formation of blood; b. Biodegradable pads at affordable prices; c. Peer education on adolescent health; d. Calcium for bone growth
questions.a: 1-d, 2-a, 3-b, 4-c. Dairy gives calcium; greens and dried fruits give iron.

questions.q: (a) Name two foods that give iron. (b) What may happen to adolescents who lack iron or vitamin B12?
questions.a: (a) Spinach, kidney beans, raisins or figs. (b) Blood-related health problems.

questions.q: (a) How should a used sanitary pad be disposed of? (b) Why does this matter beyond one's own health?
questions.a: (a) Wrap in newspaper and put in a dustbin. (b) It ensures community health and environmental cleanliness.

questions.q: Hair grows in the armpits and pubic region during adolescence. Why is cleanliness of these parts especially advised?
questions.a: Hygiene of the armpits and pubic region may protect from potential infections; adolescence brings hair growth and other body changes there.
s: Link to adolescent changes in these parts

questions.q: Vitamin B12 cannot be made in the human body. What does this mean for an adolescent's diet, and what problem may a lack of it cause?
questions.a: It must be obtained from food, so the diet must include its sources; a lack may cause blood-related problems.

questions.q: Name two government initiatives for menstrual hygiene and state one aim of each.
questions.a: Menstrual Hygiene Scheme: pads free or at reduced price for rural adolescent girls. RKSK: improves adolescent health with peer education. (Suvidha or state schemes also accepted.)

questions.q: Sneha says: "Milk, curd and paneer give calcium for bone growth, and spinach, kidney beans and raisins give calcium too." Is she right? Check her claim.
questions.a: Partly right. Milk, curd and paneer are sources of calcium for bones. But spinach, kidney beans and raisins give iron, which helps in the formation of blood, not calcium.
s: Milk, curd, paneer correctly named for calcium
Spinach, kidney beans, raisins give iron for blood

questions.q: A pamphlet says a girl who eats only milk, curd and paneer gets everything her growing body needs. Show why this cannot be right.
questions.a: They give calcium, proteins and fats but little iron; iron comes from spinach, kidney beans, raisins and figs and helps in blood formation. Lack of iron may cause blood-related problems, so variety is needed.
s: Milk foods give calcium, proteins, fats
Iron needed for blood comes from other foods
Deficiency causes problems, so variety needed

questions.q: Write a one-day menu of three local food items for an adolescent girl and state the nutrient each gives.
questions.a: For example curd with millets (calcium, proteins), spinach dal (iron, proteins), a few raisins (iron).

questions.q: Explain how an adolescent girl can maintain hygiene during menstruation, how used products are disposed of and how the government helps.
questions.a: She can use sanitary pads or reusable cloth pads. Used pads are wrapped in newspaper and put in a dustbin for community health and cleanliness; biodegradable pads are environment-friendly. Government help: Menstrual Hygiene Scheme, RKSK, Suvidha Sanitary Napkin Initiative, state schemes such as Shuchi in Karnataka.

questions.q: A school nutrition poster lists: (i) milk, curd, paneer: calcium, proteins, fats; (ii) spinach, kidney beans, raisins, figs: iron; (iii) proteins and carbohydrates. Explain what each group does for an adolescent and why a varied diet is needed.
questions.a: Group (i): calcium helps bone growth, proteins and fats help growth and strength. Group (ii): iron helps form blood. Group (iii): proteins and carbohydrates help growth and performance in games. A varied diet is needed because no single group gives everything, and a lack of iron or B12 causes blood problems.

questions.q:
The hostel mess of a Jaipur school feeds 60 girls aged 13-15 mostly rice, dal and potatoes, with little milk or greens. Many girls look pale and tired. The warden has ₹18,000 a month. Option 1: 200 mL of milk at ₹12 per girl per day for 25 days. Option 2: spinach and kidney bean dishes at ₹9 per girl per day for 25 days.
(a) Which deficiency may the girls have?
(b) Find the cost of each option and say which option's nutrient helps their problem.
(c) Decide how to use the ₹18,000: after Option 2, how many girls can get milk for 25 days with the leftover, and why is this plan reasonable?
questions.a: (a) Iron (or vitamin B12) deficiency causing blood-related problems. (b) The milk plan costs 60 x 12 x 25 = ₹18,000; the spinach and kidney bean plan costs 60 x 9 x 25 = ₹13,500; the iron in the spinach and kidney bean dishes helps blood formation. (c) Leftover ₹4,500 / (12 x 25 = ₹300) = 15 girls; iron for everyone treats the problem and some also get calcium for bones.
s: Part (c): 15 girls with a justified plan

questions.q:
In a school's girls' toilet, a dustbin was present, yet used sanitary pads were scattered near it. The class has ₹5,200. Plan A: more bins, 4 at ₹1,250 each. Plan B: a talk on menstrual hygiene (₹800) plus newspaper sheets kept near the bin (₹400).
(a) State the correct way to dispose of a used pad.
(b) What does the scattered litter show about the problem, and why does it matter beyond the girls?
(c) Find the total cost of doing both plans and say whether the class can afford it.
(d) Choose a plan and justify it.
questions.a: (a) Wrap in newspaper and put in a dustbin. (b) The bin was there, so the problem is habit and awareness; it affects community health and cleanliness. (c) 5,000 + 1,200 = ₹6,200, which is ₹1,000 more than ₹5,200, so not affordable. (d) Plan B, since a bin already exists and the need is awareness and wrapping material.

questions.q: Regular exercise during adolescence
questions.a: keeps body and mind fit, builds stamina, boosts mood. Exercise supports health; it does not replace diet or hygiene.
o: keeps body and mind fit, builds stamina, boosts mood
stops the changes of adolescence from taking place
can take the place of a nutritious balanced diet
removes the need for personal hygiene in daily life

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a 'do' for social media?
questions.a: Sharing personal photos with virtual friends. Do not share personal photos with strangers or virtual friends.
o: Sharing personal photos with virtual friends
Being respectful and kind to others
Thinking before posting anything online
Protecting your own privacy online

questions.q: Which of these is a form of cyberbullying?
questions.a: Sharing a classmate's private details without consent. Misleading messages, false rumours and sharing personal information without consent.
o: Sharing a classmate's private details without consent
Sharing a poster on responsible social media use
Asking a teacher how to use an app responsibly
Sharing information online with the owner's consent

questions.q: Sameer, 13, gets a message from an unknown 'friend' asking for his photo and address. What should he do?
questions.a: Not share them and tell a parent or teacher. Be cautious about sharing personal information with strangers.
o: Not share them and tell a parent or teacher
Share only the photo, not the address
Share both, since the person calls himself a friend
Share them if the person says it is urgent

questions.q: In a class chat, Hina posts a false story that Manav copied in a test and others forward it. This is
questions.a: cyberbullying, as a false rumour is spread digitally. False rumours are one form of cyberbullying.
o: cyberbullying, as a false rumour is spread digitally
responsible use, as the platform is meant to share information
not bullying, as no photograph was shared in the chat
not bullying, as only classmates saw it in the chat

questions.q: After his exams Pranav feels low and stays indoors. His coach asks him to join evening football, saying it will help his mood. Which idea in the chapter supports the coach?
questions.a: Regular physical activity builds stamina and boosts mood. Exercise keeps body and mind fit and boosts mood.
o: Regular physical activity builds stamina and boosts mood
Exercise removes all mood swings from an adolescent
Exercise matters for the body but not for the mind
Playing games replaces the need for proper sleep

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Spreading false rumours through digital devices can be cyberbullying.
Statement 2: If someone bullies you online, you should keep it secret so that elders are not worried.
Statement 3: Uploading personal photos is safe if the receiver is a virtual friend.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 only. Statements 2 and 3 are false: seek help from parents and teachers, and be cautious with personal photos.
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): An adolescent should be cautious when uploading a picture online.
Reason (R): Online platforms give information and connections to many people.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion. Both true, but the reach of platforms is not the reason; the reason is privacy and misuse.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q: (a) Give two benefits of regular exercise. (b) Rahul spends every evening on his phone and does no physical activity. Which benefit is he missing and what would you suggest?
questions.a: (a) Keeps body and mind fit; builds stamina; boosts mood. (b) Stamina/mood; suggest playing a sport daily.
s: Part (b): benefit missed with a suggestion

questions.q: (a) Name two things that count as cyberbullying. (b) A photo of a classmate is forwarded to a group to mock her without her permission. Is this cyberbullying? Why?
questions.a: (a) Sending misleading messages, spreading false rumours, sharing personal information without consent. (b) Yes; personal information was shared without consent to harass her.

questions.q: Why should an adolescent be careful when uploading a picture online?
questions.a: Pictures and personal information can be misused by strangers or others; one should be cautious and protect privacy.

questions.q: Why should adolescents be thoughtful and responsible when interacting in person or on social media?
questions.a: Adolescence brings new experiences and emotions, they may mimic peers and interact online; platforms should be used for collective well-being.

questions.q: Priya thinks that asking teachers for help when bullied means she failed to handle it herself. Using the chapter, explain why asking is wise.
questions.a: The chapter says not to feel scared or helpless but to handle it wisely and seek help from parents and teachers; guidance from elders helps use platforms positively.
s: Do not feel helpless; handle wisely
Seek help from parents and teachers

questions.q: Tara posts an embarrassing photo of a classmate saying: "It is only a joke and it is my own account." Evaluate her reasoning.
questions.a: Incorrect. Sharing personal pictures or information without consent to make fun of someone is cyberbullying, whatever the account. She should think before posting and protect privacy.
s: Without consent, making fun is cyberbullying

questions.q: Write a three-line poster slogan that includes three social media 'dos' from the chapter.
questions.a: Be respectful and kind. Think before you post. Protect your privacy.

questions.q: Jay spends three hours online daily and does no sport; Ira spends one hour online and plays badminton for 45 minutes. Compare them using ideas from the chapter.
questions.a: Ira gets stamina, fitness and a better mood from exercise and uses social media in a balanced way; Jay misses these benefits and risks careless use online. A balanced life, with exercise and responsible online time, is advised.
s: Jay: missing benefits / risk of careless use

questions.q: Prepare notes for a school assembly on responsible social media use: state the dos, two cautions, what a student should do if bullied and why elders' guidance helps.
questions.a: Dos: be respectful and kind, think before posting, protect privacy. Cautions: do not share personal photos with strangers or virtual friends; be cautious uploading pictures. If bullied: do not feel scared or helpless, handle wisely, seek help from parents and teachers. Guidance from elders and teachers helps use platforms positively.

questions.q: Justify the statement: "For an adolescent, physical activity and a balanced social life are also important along with nutrition."
questions.a: Regular exercise keeps body and mind fit, builds stamina and boosts mood. A balanced social life means being polite and respectful in person and online, creating a safe environment. Using social media responsibly and seeking guidance from elders and teachers supports healthy adolescence along with a nutritious diet.

questions.q:
In Class 7B's group chat, Dev spread a false story that Anu had cheated and shared a screenshot of her private message. Anu felt scared and stopped coming to cricket practice. The teacher can include only three rules in the class pledge from: (i) think before posting, (ii) never use phones, (iii) protect privacy, (iv) be respectful and kind, (v) forward every message you receive, (vi) report misuse to a teacher.
(a) Name the behaviour shown by Dev.
(b) Which two forms of it appear in the story?
(c) What should Anu do?
(d) Choose three rules and justify them.
questions.a: (a) Cyberbullying. (b) Spreading a false rumour and sharing personal information without consent. (c) Not feel scared or helpless, handle wisely and seek help from parents and teachers. (d) E.g. (i), (iii), (iv) or (vi), since (ii) is impractical and (v) spreads rumours.

questions.q:
Ishaan, 13, joined an online group and began copying the rude comments of an older boy he admires. He also gave his address to a person he had never met. His parents can choose: Plan P: phone only for one hour each evening in the family hall. Plan Q: free phone use but football at school five days a week. Plan R: phone after homework, 30 minutes of football three days a week, and a monthly talk with a teacher.
(a) Which adolescent tendency does his copying show?
(b) Which two actions go against the social media dos and don'ts?
(c) Name two benefits of the football in Plans Q and R.
(d) Pick a plan and defend it, naming one weakness of it.
questions.a: (a) Mimicking peers. (b) Being rude instead of respectful and kind, and sharing personal information with a stranger. (c) Fitness, stamina, mood boost. (d) E.g. Plan R: combines responsible use, exercise and guidance from elders; weakness: less exercise than Q.

questions.q: Regular use of a harmful addictive substance, after a strong urge to take it again has developed, is called
questions.a: substance abuse. Addiction leads to regular use, called substance abuse.
o: substance abuse
puberty
mimicking of peers
self-exploration

questions.q: Hormones are
questions.a: chemicals made in the body that regulate growth. They are released in response to signals from the brain.
o: chemicals made in the body that regulate growth
chemicals in cigarette smoke that damage the lungs
nutrients such as proteins that come only from food
structures in the throat that make the voice hoarse

questions.q: The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan places special focus on
questions.a: preventing substance abuse among early-age children. It is by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
o: preventing substance abuse among early-age children
treating adults who are already addicted to substances
supplying free pads to girls living in rural areas
peer education on adolescent nutrition in schools

questions.q: Classmates offer Karan a gutka, saying "just one time". What is the best response?
questions.a: Say NO firmly and talk to a parent or teacher. Say NO the first time and every time.
o: Say NO firmly and talk to a parent or teacher
Try it once, since he can stop whenever he wants
Accept it so that he does not lose his friends
Say no only when his parents are watching him

questions.q: Reena's class asks why menstruation and other changes start at this age. Which explanation matches the chapter?
questions.a: Hormones released on signals from the brain regulate them. Many changes are mainly due to hormones.
o: Hormones released on signals from the brain regulate them
The changes occur because adolescents simply eat more food
The changes occur because addictive substances build up in the body
The voice box is the cause of all the other changes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
Statement 1: Hormones are released in response to signals from the brain.
Statement 2: Hormones affect only the body and never mood or behaviour.
Statement 3: Menstruation and other signs of puberty are mainly due to hormones.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 only. Statement 2 is false: some hormones influence mood and behaviour.
o: 2 only
1 only
3 only
1 and 3 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Someone who is addicted today might have started with 'just one time'.
Reason (R): Addictive substances create a strong urge to take them again and again.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion. The urge to repeat explains how one try becomes regular use.
o: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Hormones are produced in different parts of the body.
Reason (R): Hormones are released only when the brain sends no signal.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Assertion is true but Reason is false. A is true; R is false because they are released in response to signals from the brain.
o: Assertion is true but Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion
Assertion is false but Reason is true

questions.q: (a) Name two harmful substances adolescents may be pressured to consume. (b) State two health problems they can cause.
questions.a: (a) Tobacco, gutka, cigarettes, beedi, alcohol or illegal drugs. (b) Breathing difficulties, memory loss, lung damage.

questions.q: (a) What is the National De-addiction Helpline number? (b) A friend has begun using such substances regularly. Whom would you advise him to approach?
questions.a: (a) 14446. (b) Family, friends, parents or teachers; counselling and medical advice.

questions.q: Define hormones and give one effect they have on an adolescent.
questions.a: Chemicals produced in the body that regulate growth and development; e.g. they cause menstruation or influence mood and behaviour.

questions.q: What does the advice "Say NO the first time and every time" mean?
questions.a: Refuse harmful substances at the first offer and every later offer, firmly and confidently, without giving in to 'just one time'.
s: Refuse at first offer and always

questions.q: Explain how a person who tries a substance 'just one time' may end up using it regularly.
questions.a: The substance is addictive, so a strong urge develops to take it again and again; over time this becomes regular use called substance abuse.
s: Leads to regular use / substance abuse

questions.q: Which ministry launched the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, and whose active participation does it seek?
questions.a: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; the youth, women and the community.

questions.q: Vikas says: "Trying a cigarette once is harmless, because I can stop whenever I want." Evaluate his claim.
questions.a: Wrong. Such substances are addictive; a strong urge to repeat develops and regular use becomes substance abuse. They also harm health, so one should say NO.
s: Leads to substance abuse and harm

questions.q: Write a three-line conversation in which a student firmly refuses peers who offer a harmful substance.
questions.a: Peer: Try it once. Student: No, I will not; it is harmful and addictive. I am staying away and will talk to my teacher if you keep pushing.
s: Firm and confident with a reason

questions.q: State three roles of hormones in adolescence as given in the chapter.
questions.a: They regulate growth and development; they cause changes such as menstruation and signs of puberty; they are released on signals from the brain; some influence mood and behaviour.

questions.q: Explain why adolescents should avoid harmful substances: name them, the problems they cause, what addiction and substance abuse mean, and where to seek help.
questions.a: Tobacco, gutka, cigarettes, beedi, alcohol and illegal drugs harm physical and mental health. They cause breathing difficulties, memory loss and lung damage. Addiction is a strong urge to take them again and again, leading to regular use called substance abuse. Say NO and seek help from family, friends, parents or teachers; counselling and medical advice help.
s: Say NO the first time and every time

questions.q: Answer the 'why' question of adolescence: what are hormones, how are they released, what changes do they cause, and how do they connect physical and emotional changes?
questions.a: Hormones are chemicals produced in different parts of the body and released at the right time in response to signals from the brain. They regulate growth and development and cause menstruation and signs of puberty. Some also influence mood and behaviour, which connects the physical changes to the emotional ones.
s: Released on signals from the brain

questions.q:
A Bhopal school holds a Nasha Mukt awareness week. Karthik tells his class that his 17-year-old cousin began with a cigarette 'just one time' at a party. Now he gets breathless on stairs, forgets his homework, and has a stomach upset after meals. The school may either (X) run sessions for Class 6-8 with youth volunteers or (Y) hold one assembly for all classes with the helpline displayed.
(a) Which two of the cousin's problems match the chapter's list of effects?
(b) Why can't he stop easily?
(c) Whom should Karthik ask his cousin to approach?
(d) Choose X or Y and justify using the Abhiyaan's focus.
questions.a: (a) Breathing difficulty and memory loss. (b) The substance is addictive and creates a strong urge to repeat. (c) Family, friends, parents or teachers; counselling and medical advice; helpline 14446. (d) X, since the focus is prevention among early-age children; or Y with the reason that it reaches older students and shows the helpline.
s: Part (a): breathing difficulty and memory loss

questions.q:
In class Pooja asks why changes like menstruation and a changing voice begin at this age. Their teacher says that certain chemicals made in the body are responsible. Pooja then says: "So my mood swings are just hormones and I can do nothing." Sunil replies: "Hormones influence mood, but I can still choose what I do about it."
(a) Name these chemicals.
(b) In response to what are they released?
(c) Name two things they regulate or influence.
(d) Which part of Pooja's statement is right, and what would you add from the chapter?
questions.a: (a) Hormones. (b) Signals from the brain. (c) Growth and development; menstruation; mood and behaviour. (d) She is right that hormones influence mood, but the chapter shows adolescents can handle emotions through positive activities and guidance.
s: Part (d): partly right, with positive handling added
